Tsar of Russia from 1682 to 1725, who set out to remake his country on Western lines and turned it into a great European power.

He became tsar as a boy and ruled alone from 1696. In 1697 and 1698 he travelled through Western Europe with the Grand Embassy. He came home determined to change Russia.

  • He built Russia's first real navy.
  • He fought the Great Northern War against Sweden, won at Poltava in 1709, and gained the Baltic coast.
  • He founded Saint Petersburg in 1703 and made it the new capital.
  • He ordered nobles to shave their beards and wear Western clothes, set up a Table of Ranks for state service, and put the church under a state board.

In 1721 he took the title of emperor, and the Tsardom of Muscovy became the Russian Empire. His reforms were forced through with heavy taxes and forced labour, and his own son Alexei died in prison after Peter had him tried for treason. Catherine the Great later saw herself as his heir.
sum: Tsar of Russia from 1682 to 1725, who set out to remake his country on Western lines and turned it into a great European power.
